label: Robert T. Bigelow
narrative: Bigelow privatised the problem. A Las Vegas real-estate developer who built the Budget Suites of America extended-stay chain, he founded the National Institute for Discovery Science in 1995 as a privately funded research institute studying aerial phenomena, animal mutilations and related anomalies, and staffed it with people carrying federal clearances and federal programme histories - Hal Puthoff from the CIA/DIA remote-viewing programmes, Colonel John Alexander from Army INSCOM and Los Alamos, the biochemist Colm Kelleher, and Jacques Vallee. In 1996 he bought the 480-acre Sherman ranch in Uintah County, Utah - Skinwalker Ranch - as a permanent instrumented field site, requiring the sellers to sign non-disclosure conditions as part of the purchase. He told the Deseret News in August 1998, in his first interview on the subject, that the phenomena had continued and that 'we wouldn't be there just for the weather,' while declining to discuss specifics. NIDS operated a public reporting hotline and a veterinary necropsy response capability. He shut NIDS down in 2004 but kept the ranch. Three years later a senior Defense Intelligence Agency official wrote to him about Skinwalker, and that contact became the AAWSAP contract. Bigelow is therefore the mechanism by which a private billionaire's field programme was converted into a federally funded intelligence programme without changing the personnel - which is the single most important structural fact about how this subject was handled after Blue Book closed.
